phrases.arabic: مَا اقْدِرْتُ أرِد عَلَيْك قَبْلِ شْوَايَة

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Hi Lina, what's new?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بِخَيْر. اتَّصَلْتُ عَلَيْك قَبْلِ شْوَايَة بَس الْخَطّ كَانَ مَشْغُول
dialogue.transliteration: il-7amdella bi-khair. ittasalt 3aleek gabil shwaya bas il-khatt kaan mashghool
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: إي، كُنْتُ أتَكَلَّم مَعَ أَخِي. آسِف مَا اقْدِرْتُ أرِد عَلَيْك
dialogue.transliteration: ee, kuntu atkallam ma3a akh. aasif ma agdartu arid 3aleek
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: وَلاَ يِهِمَّك. أَبْغِي أحَكِي مَعَك عَنِ الْمَوْعِد
dialogue.transliteration: wala yihimmak. abgha a7aki ma3ak 3an il-maw3id
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. I want to talk to you about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر، خَلِّينِي أحَكِي بِسُرْعَة قَبْلِ لاَ يِنْقَطِع الْخَطّ
dialogue.transliteration: hadir, khallini a7aki bi-sur3a gabil la yingata3 il-khatt
dialogue.english: Okay, let me talk fast before the call cuts off.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: لاَ لاَ، خَلاَص، انْقَطَع. اقْدِرِي تِتَّصِلِي عَلَيّ بَعِد شْوَايَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: la la, khalaas, ingata3. agdari titsilii 3alay ba3ad shwaya?
dialogue.english: No no, it's over, it got cut off. Can you call me back in a bit?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر، زَيِّن إِنَّك اتَّصَلْتَ أَصْلاً. بِتَّصِل عَلَيْك
dialogue.transliteration: hadir, zayin innak ittasalt aslan. bitsil 3aleek
dialogue.english: Okay, good that you called at all. I'll call you back.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll wait for you.

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: In Yemen, a call usually opens with "آلو" and the caller introduces themselves. Quick greetings like "شنو أخبارك" are common before explaining the reason for the call. Ending with a quick goodbye and "الله يحفظك" is polite and keeps the call brief.

exercises.prompt: You pick up the phone and hear: "آلُّو؟". Answer naturally, asking who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من فضلك من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Arabic, but far more formal than the ordinary way of answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "شنو فيك" is the everyday Yemeni way to ask who is calling.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you on the phone: "شْنُو أَخْبَارَك؟". Say that everything is fine, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام، ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; a spoken reply is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" almost always appears somewhere in the answer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ما اقدرت _____ عليك قبل شوايه." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

too_formal.feedback: Understandable, but "رد" is the word actually used on the phone in Yemeni speech.

exercises.tip: "رد على" is the everyday phrase for answering someone's call.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ الخط علي وأنا أتكلم معك." Meaning: The call got cut off on me while I was talking to you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a technical report, not something a person says on the phone.

exercises.tip: "انقطع الخط" or "قطع الخط" both describe a dropped call.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Yemeni Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more formal than how people actually say it.

exercises.tip: "خلص / خلصت" covers running out of almost anything: credit, battery, patience.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية شبكية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: Correct but reads like a technician's report, not spoken Yemeni.

exercises.tip: "شبaka" is the everyday word for phone signal; "هنيه" is the Yemeni "here".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "خلص" is the word used in everyday speech, not "انتهى".

exercises.tip: "رصيد" is prepaid phone credit.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله، من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: Too long for picking up a phone; the short "آلو" is what is said.

exercises.tip: "آلو" answers the phone; the other phrases come once the call is already going.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مشغول / كان / الخط".

too_formal.feedback: That would be an unusual, technical way to say the line was busy.

exercises.tip: "الخط" comes first, then "كان", then how the line was.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "عليّ / بعد شوايه / تتصل / اقدر".

too_formal.item: هل بإمكانك معاودة الاتصال بي لاحقاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is the formal written version, not the spoken order of words.

exercises.tip: "اقدر" (can) opens it, then the verb, then when.

reply.english: In front of the main entrance.

phrases.english: We'll meet at the Great Mosque.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Lina, where should we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: شْنُو رَأيْك نِلْتَقِي فِي الْمَقْهَى عِنْد الْبَازَار؟
dialogue.transliteration: shnoo ra2yak niltagi fi l-magha 3ind il-bazaar?
dialogue.english: What do you think, shall we meet at the cafe near the market?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Good idea. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Okay, where exactly, in front of the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll see you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Great, I'll definitely be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Don't be late on me, Lina.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: وَلاَ يِهِمَّك، وَإِذَا تَأخَّرْتُ بِتَّصِل عَلَيْك
dialogue.transliteration: wala yihimmak, w idha ta2akhart bitsil 3aleek
dialogue.english: Don't worry, and if I'm late I'll call you.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.

response.english: In front of the main entrance.

pair.english: What do you think, shall we go together?

lessons.culture: In Yemen people usually arrange to meet at markets (bazaars), cafes, or mosques rather than giving street addresses. Confirming the exact spot at the entrance is important. A quick greeting and the time matter more than lengthy planning.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "وَيْن نِلْتَقِي؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct, but far more formal than a casual suggestion.

exercises.tip: Simple and direct is best for everyday Yemeni speech.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "أي سَاعَة تِنَاسِبْك؟". Say that 7 o'clock is good for you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a written appointment confirmation, not spoken.

exercises.tip: "زينة" is the Yemeni "good" for times and things.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أشوفك _____ المدخل الرئيسي." Meaning: I'll see you at the main entrance.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "قدام" or "عند" is what is actually said in Yemeni speech.

exercises.tip: "قدام" means "in front of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إِذَا تَأخَّرْتَ _____ عَلَيّ." Meaning: If you're late, call me.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but very formal written Arabic, not how it is said.

exercises.tip: "اتصل علي" (call on me) is how Yemeni says "call me".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Yemeni Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is a formal written notice style, not spoken Yemeni.

exercises.tip: "لا" + present-tense verb is the everyday negative command.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically identical but uses the formal future "سـ" instead of the spoken "ب".

exercises.tip: "ب" + present-tense verb makes the everyday future in Yemeni speech.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "What time suits you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiffer than the everyday spoken question.

exercises.tip: "أي ساعة" is the Yemeni way to ask about time.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's meet at the cafe"?

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct classical form, but not how it's said in conversation.

exercises.tip: Direct statements are preferred in Yemeni everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "سبعة / زينة / الساعة".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more elaborate than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: The time comes first, then the check word "زينة" at the end.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "المدخل الرئيسي / قدام / أشوفك".

too_formal.item: سألتقي بك أمام المدخل الرئيسي للمبنى
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a much longer, written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "أشوفك" (I'll see you) usually opens the sentence, then the place.

phrases.arabic: نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
phrases.transliteration: nigdar niltagi ba3ad ith-thuhr badal iS-Subh?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Hello Samer, I want to change the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: What happened? Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: إي، طَرَا عَلَيّ شِي فِي الْبَيْت وَمَا اقْدِر أِجِي الْيَوْم
dialogue.transliteration: ee, tara 3alay shi fi l-beet w ma agdar iji l-yoom
dialogue.english: Yeah, something came up at home and I can't come today.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: وَلاَ مِشْكِلَة، نِأجِّل لِبُكْرَة. بَس نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala mishkla, ni2ajjil li-bukra. bas nigdar niltagi ba3ad ith-thuhr badal iS-Subh?
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to tomorrow. But can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، بَعِد الظُّهْر أَحْسَن لِي كِمَان
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ba3ad ith-thuhr a7san li kiman
dialogue.english: Great, the afternoon is better for me too.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Thanks, sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: وَلاَ يِهِمَّك، هَيِّك بِصِير. الْمَكَان الْحَيْن نِفْسُ الْمَكَان؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala yihimmak, hayik bisiir. il-makaan il-7iin nafs il-makaan?
dialogue.english: Don't worry, it happens. Is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: لاَ، غَيِّرْنَا الْمَكَان، نِلْتَقِي عِنْد الْمَقْهَى الْجَدِيد
dialogue.transliteration: la, ghayarna l-makaan, niltagi 3ind il-magha l-jadid
dialogue.english: No, we changed the place, we'll meet at the new cafe.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر، بِحْفِظ الْعِنْوَان. شُكْرًا عِنِّك خَبْرِتِينِي بِدْرِي
dialogue.transliteration: hadir, bi7fidh il-3unwaan. shukran 3innik khabbritni badri
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll save the address. Thanks for letting me know early.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: الله يحفظك، أِشُوفَك بُكْرَة بَعِد الظُّهْر
dialogue.transliteration: allah yuhfithik, ashuufak bukra ba3ad ith-thuhr
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you tomorrow afternoon.

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.

pair.arabic: نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
pair.transliteration: nigdar niltagi ba3ad ith-thuhr badal iS-Subh?
pair.english: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

response.english: Yes, the afternoon is better for me.

pair.english: Is the place still the same place?

lessons.culture: In Yemen, plans often change due to family matters, prayer times, and daily needs, and rearranging at short notice is normal and expected. A quick apology like "آسف عالتغيير" shows respect, and the response "ولا يهمك" indicates there are no hard feelings. Friday is often adjusted around the Friday prayer.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: "آسِف عَالتَّغْيِير الْمُفاجِي". Tell them not to worry about it.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the short spoken reassurance.

exercises.tip: "ولا يهمك" is the standard easy way to say "don't worry about it".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "نِقْدِر نِأجِّل لِبُكْرَة؟". Agree, saying no problem.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but this is the written, not the spoken, register.

exercises.tip: "ولا مشكلة" is a very common easy agreement phrase.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ عليّ شِي وَمَا اقْدِر أِجِي." Meaning: Something came up for me and I can't come.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but redundant and bookish; the spoken version is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "طرا علي شي" is the fixed everyday Yemeni phrase for "something came up".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر _____ الصُّبْح؟" Meaning: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal than the short spoken "بدل".

exercises.tip: "بدل" means "instead of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Yemeni Arabic: "I can't come today."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but more formal than the everyday spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "ما اقدر" is the everyday Yemeni "I can't".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can we postpone to tomorrow?"

too_formal.item: هل يمكننا تأجيل الموعد إلى الغد؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a longer, written-style question.

exercises.tip: "نقدر" + present-tense verb is the everyday Yemeni "can we...".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Is the place still the same place?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal phrasing than the spoken question.

exercises.tip: "الحين" means "now" in Yemeni speech.

exercises.prompt: Which is a natural apology for changing plans suddenly?

too_formal.item: أعتذر منكم عن هذا التغيير الطارئ
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but stiff and overly formal for a friend.

exercises.tip: "آسف" (man) / "آسفة" (woman) عالتغيير المفاجي fits a casual apology.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "لبكره / نأجل / نقدر".

too_formal.item: هل من الممكن أن نؤجل الأمر إلى الغد
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a much longer formal question.

exercises.tip: "نقدر" opens the question, then the verb, then the day.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الصبح / بدل / بعد الظهر / نلتقي / نقدر".
exercises.answer: نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح
accepted: نِقْدِر نِلْتَقِي بَعِد الظُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح

too_formal.item: هل بإمكاننا اللقاء بعد الظهيرة عوضاً عن الصباح؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "نقدر" (can we) opens it, then the verb, then the two times being compared.

phrases.english: Can you pass him a message? (to a woman)

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: لاَ، مِش هُنِيهْ الْحَيْن، طَلَع عِند الْبَازَار
dialogue.transliteration: la, mish hunih il-7iin, tala3 3ind il-bazaar
dialogue.english: No, he's not here right now, he went to the market.

dialogue.speaker: رامي
dialogue.english: Ah, roughly when will he be back?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: مَا أَعْرِف بِالضَّبْط، بَعِد شْوَايَة إِنْ شَاءَ الله
dialogue.transliteration: ma a3rif biḍ-ḍabT, ba3ad shwaya in shaa2 allah
dialogue.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit God willing.

dialogue.speaker: رامي
dialogue.english: Okay, can you pass a message to him for me?

dialogue.speaker: رامي
dialogue.arabic: قُولِي لَهُ رَامِي اتَّصَل، وَيِتَّصِل عَلَيّ إِذَا فاضِي
dialogue.transliteration: qooli lahu Raami ittasil, w yittsil 3alay idha faadi
dialogue.english: Tell him Rami called, and to call me if he's free.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

dialogue.speaker: رامي
dialogue.english: Does he have my number?

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: مَا أَعْرِف، خَلِّينِي آخُذ رَقْمَك احْتِيَاط
dialogue.transliteration: ma a3rif, khallini aakhudh ragmak i7tiyaat
dialogue.english: I don't know, let me take your number just in case.

dialogue.speaker: رامي
dialogue.english: Here you go, thanks a lot for the favor.

dialogue.speaker: ليينة
dialogue.arabic: الله يُحْفِظَك، بِوَصِّلُو الْخَبَر أوْلِ مَا يِفُوت
dialogue.transliteration: allah yuhfithak, biwassilo l-khabar awwal ma yfut
dialogue.english: You're very welcome, I'll pass him the news as soon as he's in.

response.english: No, he's not here right now.
I don't know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you take a message for me?

lessons.culture: In Yemen, a family member often answers the phone and takes messages, and the caller may ask after the family before delivering their message. "الله يحفظك" is the standard thank-you for a favor, and "أيوه" (yes) is the most common agreement word. Politeness and respect for the messenger is important.

exercises.prompt: Someone calling asks: "سَامِر مَوْجُود؟" but he is out. Say he's not here right now.

too_formal.item: لا، هو غير موجود في الحالية
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but overly formal for a family member answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "هنيه الحين" is the everyday Yemeni way to say "not here right now".

exercises.prompt: A caller asks: "مَتَى بِيرْجَع؟". Say you don't know exactly, in a bit.

too_formal.item: لا أعرف على وجه التحديد، في وقت قريب
too_formal.feedback: Correct but overly formal for spoken Yemeni.

exercises.tip: "بعد شوايه" is a vague but common Yemeni time reference.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "اقْدِرِي _____ لَهُ رِسَالَة؟" Meaning: Can you take a message for him?

too_formal.feedback: Understandable but "توصلي" is the everyday Yemeni verb for passing a message.

exercises.tip: "توصل" means "to deliver" in Yemeni.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ لَهُ أوْلِ مَا يِوصِل." Meaning: I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal than the everyday Yemeni phrase.

exercises.tip: "بخبره" (I'll tell him) is simple and direct.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Yemeni Arabic: "When will he be back?"

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but more formal than the everyday Yemeni question.

exercises.tip: "متى" (when) + "بيرجع" (will return) is the everyday Yemeni question.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Do you have my number?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal than the everyday Yemeni question.

exercises.tip: "عندك" is the everyday Yemeni way to ask "do you have".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Can you take a message for me?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal than the everyday Yemeni phrase.

exercises.tip: "توصل" is the verb for delivering messages.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to agree to take a message?

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal. "أيوه" (yes) is the everyday Yemeni word.

exercises.tip: "أيوه" is the most common Yemeni "yes", followed immediately by "شنو الرسالة".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "يفوت / ما / أول / الخبر / بوصله".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but much more elaborate than the simple Yemeni phrase.

exercises.tip: "بوصله" opens, then the news, then "أول ما يفوت" (as soon as he's in).

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "محفوظ / الحين / رقمي / عندي".

too_formal.item: نعم لديّ رقمك محفوظ في الذاكرة
too_formal.feedback: Correct but much more elaborate than the simple everyday response.

exercises.tip: Start with "إي" (yes), then "عندي" (I have), then the thing, then "محفوظ" (saved).

challenge.title: Plan a Phone Call and Meeting
challenge.instructions: You are going to call your friend and plan a meeting with them. In your conversation, include: answering the phone, asking how they are, suggesting a meeting location and time, and confirming the details. Use the vocabulary and structures from this unit.
required_elements: A suggestion for where to meet
Confirmation of the location and time

dialogue.speaker: أنت
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: صديقك
dialogue.english: Hello, it's Ali. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: أنت
dialogue.arabic: آلُّو عَلِي، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بِخَيْر. أَبْغِي نِلْتَقِي بُكْرَة، وَيْن تِبْغِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: aaloo 3ali, il-7amdella bi-khair. abgha niltagi bukra, wayn tibgha?
dialogue.english: Hello Ali, all good thank God. I want to meet tomorrow, where do you want?

dialogue.speaker: صديقك
dialogue.english: What do you think about the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: أنت
dialogue.english: Great. What time?

dialogue.speaker: صديقك
dialogue.english: 7 o'clock?

dialogue.speaker: أنت
dialogue.english: Okay. I'll see you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: صديقك
dialogue.english: Great, take care!
